sentences.text: The claimants are wife, son, father and mother of the deceased Satish Kolhar.

The claimants have filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation for the accidental death of Satish Kolhar occurred on 08.02.2017 involving car bearing No.KA-48/M-6859 claiming compensation of Rs.1,45,62,500/-.
4. On issuance of notice, respondents appeared through their counsels.

The respondent No.1 denying the petition averments, admitted the accident and denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the car and contended that the driver was holding a valid driving license and car was insured with respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2-insurer denied validity of driving license and disputed the dependency of son and father of the deceased.
Thus, prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
The claimant No.1-wife of the deceased examined herself as PW-1 and got marked Exs.P-1 to P-30.
Respondent No.1 has not led evidence.
Respondent No.2 examined its official as RW-2 and marked Exs.R1 to R4.

The Tribunal based on material evidence on record awarded total compensation of Rs.58,28,632/- with interest at 9% p.a. on the following heads:
Sl.
 Heads of Compensation Amount No.
1.
Towards loss of dependency 57,58,632.00 2.
Towards loss of estate 15,000.00 3.
Towards Consortium 40,000.00 4.
Towards Funeral Expenses 15,000.00  Total 58,28,632.00 6.
While awarding the compensation, the Tribunal considered the annual income of the deceased at Rs.7,13,878/-(Business income Rs.3,83,798/- + Agriculture income Rs.3,30,080/-).
The Tribunal considered the age of the deceased as 51 years and added 10% of income towards future prospects, deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses and applied multiplier 11.
The claimants in their appeal are seeking enhancement of compensation and the insurer is seeking reduction of compensation.

8. Heard Shri. Nagangouda R. Kuppelur for the appellant/insurer, Shri. Shrinivas B. Naik for claimants Shri. B.G. Indi, learned counsel for respondent No.5-owner of the vehicle and perused the appeal papers along with original records.

Learned counsel for the appellant/insurer submits that the Tribunal committed an error in assessing the income on the basis of Ex.P9-income tax returns for the assessment year 2016-17.
Learned counsel further contends that the average income as per three assessment years income prior to the date of accident is to be considered.
Learned counsel contended that returns of income are filed on behalf of the company and it cannot be considered to determine the income of the deceased.
No proof of Agricultural income is produced to consider the Agricultural income.
It is further contended that the NC: 2024:KHC-D:993-DB second claimant is not dependant.
Claimant No.2 is a party to the compromise decree in O.S. No.78/2015 wherein he was allotted 13 acres of land and also contended that award of interest at 9% is on the higher side.
10. Per contra, learned counsel for the claimants submits that age of the deceased is to be considered at 49 years and average income of three assessment years is to be considered.
It is further submitted that as per PAN card, the age of the deceased is to be considered at 49 years as on the date of the accident and accordingly multiplier has to be applied.

It is further submitted that the 2nd and 3rd claimants were dependants on the earnings of the deceased and to be considered as dependants and hence, applicable deduction would be 1/4th as against 1/3rd made by the Tribunal.
Considering the age of the deceased at 49 years, future prospects is to be awarded at 25%.

On the above submission,
prays for enhancement of compensation.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of appeal papers along with original records, the points that would fall for consideration in these appeals are as follows.

i. Whether the Tribunal is justified in assessing the income of the deceased by considering the Income tax returns for the assessment year 2016-17 instead of considering average income for the assessment years 2014-15, 2015-16 and 2016-17?
ii. Whether the Tribunal is right in awarding interest at the rate of 9% p.a.?
iii. Whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just?
12. The answer to the above points would be negative for the following reasons.
13. As stated above, the accident has occurred on 08.02.2017 involving car bearing No.KA-48/M-6859.
The death of deceased Satish Kolhar due to the said accident is not in dispute in this appeal.
Both the appellants are NC: 2024:KHC-D:993-DB before this Court disputing quantum of compensation.

The deceased was carrying on the business in the name of Kolhar Yatri Nivas Pvt.
Ltd.
The contention of the insurer is that a return of income at Exs.P7 to P9 is on behalf of the company and not an individual income of the deceased.
As seen from Exs.P7 to P9-Income tax returns for the assessment year 2014-15, 2015-16 and 2016-17, the returns have been filed in the status of individual.
Hence, we hold that Exs.P7 to P9 are the returns of income of the deceased in his individual capacity.

The Tribunal while determining the income of the deceased instead of considering returns of income for the assessment year 2016-17, ought to have considered average of Smt.Suman W/O. Accordingly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Another, 1/4th is to be deducted towards personal expenses.

sentences.text: 15. The petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are son and father of the deceased.
The dependency is to be considered as on - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:993-DB the date of death.
The 2nd claimant-son was not having any independent income and he was a student as on the date of accident.
Hence, the 2nd claimant has to be considered as dependant.
The 3rd claimant being father was aged 79 years and dependant on the deceased.
The Tribunal finding that the father is having independent source of income from agriculture is without any basis.
Considering the age of claimant No.3-father he has to be considered as dependant of the deceased.
16. Though, the claimants have contended that the deceased was aged 49 years, no material has been placed to substantiate the age of the deceased.

The Tribunal has rightly, by placing reliance on Smt.Suman W/O. Satish Kolhar vs Sudhir S/O. Balachandrappa Kolhar on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117358476/

In view of considering the age of the deceased at 51 years, the claimants are entitled for future prospects at 10%
to be added to the total income.
17. The reliance on the compromise in O.S.No.78/2015 by the insurer to contend that - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:993-DB petitioner/claimant No.2 was not dependant is not correct.
The compromise is subsequent to the date of death and the dependency as on the date of death has to be considered.
As on the date of death, 2nd claimant was a student and has no independent source of income.
Hence 2nd claimant has to be considered as dependant.
18. The Tribunal committed an error in not awarding sum of Rs.40,000/- under the head of consortium to all the claimants.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram & Others, all the claimants being wife, son and parents are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head consortium.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.76,58,816/- as against 58,28,632/- awarded by the Tribunal.
21. The Tribunal has awarded the compensation with the interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit of the compensation amount.

As per Section 150 of the MVC Act,

sentences.text: interest payable on the award amount is as per law relating to the interest.
Interest Tax Act is not applicable in the present case.
Section 34 of CPC provides for interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

Considering the above aspect and also the prevailing rate of interest, we deem it appropriate to - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:993-DB award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. as against 9% p.a. as awarded by the Tribunal.
In the result, we proceed to pass the following ORDER a) Both appeals are allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.76,58,816/-as against Rs.58,28,632/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount of Rs.18,30,184/- will bear interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.

d) The respondent-Insurance Company  shall deposit the enhanced  compensation amount with accrued  - 15 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:993-DB interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) Apportionment, deposit and  disbursement of the enhanced compensation amount shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
f) Registry to transmit the records to the Tribunal forthwith.
g) Draw modified award accordingly.
